name: SafestClaw
vibe_summary: A zero-cost, LLM-optional OpenClaw alternative that leans on classic ML intent-matching and deterministic actions instead of language models. Its pitch is minimal prompt-injection surface, offline-first operation, and $0 monthly cost.
best_for: Users who want OpenClaw-style features without LLM API bills
Privacy-conscious users wanting offline, deterministic actions
Tinkerers comfortable learning command documentation instead of free-form chat
avoid_if: You need robust free-form conversational AI out of the box
You want a large plugin ecosystem and community support
You need battle-tested multi-user or team deployments
openclaw_advantages: No LLM required for most features, so $0 default operating cost
Minimal prompt-injection surface due to deterministic intent matching
Runs on modest hardware across Linux, macOS, and Windows
openclaw_disadvantages: Far smaller community, stars, and ecosystem than OpenClaw
Free-form chat quality depends on optional LLM setup that has had config bugs
Requires learning documentation/commands when running LLM-free
Single-maintainer project with higher bus-factor risk
confidence_summary: Evidence is solid from the README and detailed recent commits, but community sentiment is thin — the single Reddit match is irrelevant and web results mostly reference OpenClaw itself. Ratings for ecosystem and sentiment carry meaningful uncertainty.

overview_markdown:
SafestClaw positions itself as the zero-cost, security-minded alternative to OpenClaw. Its core architectural bet is that most assistant tasks — weather lookups, news summaries from 50+ sources, research queries against arXiv/WolframAlpha, blogging, code security audits — don't actually need a large language model. Instead it uses classic ML intent and semantic matching to route commands to deterministic, auditable actions, with an LLM (Anthropic, Ollama, etc.) as an optional layer for free-form chat.

The project ships as a pip-installable Python package (`pip install safestclaw`, run via `python -m safestclaw`) with a CLI, localhost web UI, Telegram integration, and optional MCP support. It runs offline by default, stores config in `~/.safestclaw/config.yaml`, and works across Linux, macOS, and Windows — including auto-start via systemd, launchd, Task Scheduler, or cron.

Recent commits show active maintenance focused on reliability: fixing config-path bugs that caused state loss across service launches, ensuring `setup ai` reliably enables the NLU layer, surfacing LLM provider errors to users instead of silently falling back to canned replies, and tightening intent regexes that misrouted chat. Compared to OpenClaw, it trades the massive ecosystem and polished agent experience for determinism, privacy, and zero API cost.
